record.paper_title: The combinatorics of discrete time-trees: theory and open problems
record.context_brief: Distance complexity in discrete time-tree graphs
record.original_question: A discrete time-tree is a rooted binary phylogenetic tree on a fixed labeled leaf set in which every node is assigned a distinct non-negative integer time and each child has smaller time than its parent. The paper studies graph families on such trees, including DtTm, DtTum, RNNI, and RNNIu, where two trees are adjacent when one can be obtained from the other by one allowed local move such as changing the length of one event interval by 1, swapping the ranks of two nodes that bound a unit-length interval, or performing a nearest-neighbor interchange move on a unit-length interval, with graph-specific restrictions. Given two discrete time-trees in one of these graph families, what is the computational complexity of computing their graph distance, meaning the minimum number of allowed moves needed to transform one tree into the other?

evidence.quote: A discrete time-tree is a tree such that all its nodes are assigned distinct times from the set of non-negative integers and every node has a smaller time than its parent

Two trees T and R are adjacent in DtTm if R can be obtained from T by one of three operations: a length move performed on interval I, swapping the rank of two nodes x and y on interval I or an NNI move performed on interval I
Problem 1 What is the complexity of computing the distance between two discrete time-trees?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a fixed finite set of leaf labels with |X| ≥ 2. A discrete time-tree on X is a rooted binary tree whose leaves are bijectively labeled by X and in which every node (internal node or leaf) is assigned a distinct non-negative integer time, such that every non-root node has a strictly smaller time than its parent and the times of the leaves are prescribed (e.g., all equal to 0, or given as part of the input). For a discrete time-tree T with internal-node times t_1 < t_2 < … < t_k, the i-th event interval is the set of edges of T that are crossed by a horizontal line at any time strictly between t_i and t_{i+1} (with the 0-th interval lying below t_1 and the k-th interval lying above t_k); call an event interval a unit interval if t_{i+1} − t_i = 1.

Define four graphs whose vertices are discrete time-trees on X:

(1) DtTm: T and T' are adjacent iff T' is obtained from T by exactly one of the following local moves:
   (a) length move: increase or decrease the length of one event interval by 1 (subject to the times remaining a valid strictly increasing sequence of distinct non-negative integers);
   (b) rank move: choose a unit-length event interval that is bounded above and below by two internal nodes x and y, and swap the times (ranks) of x and y;
   (c) NNI move: perform a nearest-neighbor interchange across an edge belonging to a unit-length event interval.

(2) DtTum: the subgraph of DtTm induced on discrete time-trees in which all event intervals have unit length (only rank and NNI moves apply).

(3) RNNI: same as DtTm but with length moves disallowed (only rank and NNI moves are permitted).

(4) RNNIu: the analogue of RNNI restricted to ultrametric/unit-interval discrete time-trees.

For each of these four graph families G ∈ {DtTm, DtTum, RNNI, RNNIu}, determine the computational complexity of the following problem: given two vertices T, T' of G as input, compute the graph distance d_G(T, T'), i.e., the minimum number of allowed moves needed to transform T into T'.
artifact.status_search_result: For the RNNI graph (rank and NNI moves on ranked phylogenetic trees), Collienne and Gavryushkin (J. Math. Biol., 2021) showed that the FINDPATH algorithm computes shortest paths/distances in O(n^2) time, giving a polynomial-time algorithm and resolving the RNNI case. Subsequent work on a weighted variant RNNI(ρ) shows the shortest-path problem is NP-hard at one extreme (RNNI(0), where it reduces to NNI) and quadratic at the other (RNNI(1)). Complexity for the discrete time-tree variants DtTm and DtTum (which also include length moves on event intervals) does not appear to be settled in the literature found. Hence the problem is partially solved: settled for RNNI (polynomial), open in general.

status_evidence.title: Computing nearest neighbour interchange distances between ranked phylogenetic trees
status_evidence.snippet: the worst-case time complexity of the shortest path problem in the RNNI graph on trees with n leaves is O(n^2)
status_evidence.claim: RNNI distance is computable in polynomial (quadratic) time.

status_evidence.title: Geometry of Ranked Nearest Neighbour Interchange Space of Phylogenetic Trees
status_evidence.snippet: shortest path problem is NP-hard in RNNI(0) and quadratic in RNNI(1)
status_evidence.claim: Complexity of weighted RNNI variants ranges from quadratic to NP-hard depending on weights.
